scope: Theorem 4.1 (A joint estimate given base paths) of the manuscript “Conditional information under deterministic coordinate sweeps” (preprints/Conditional-information-under-deterministic-coordinate-sweeps-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ad4125b0a60530a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < p < 1, and put q = 1 + p 2 , ρ = 1 + q 2 = 3 + p 4 , cp = − 1 8 log2 ρ, b = b(p) = & 10 cp ' . Run independent fair matching switches on V = Fd 2 in any fixed cyclic order of its d coordinate directions, from any deterministic starting deck. Let n = 2d, T = 2bd, and fix a set B of r0 labels and an ordered list (a1, . . . , ak) of other distinct labels, where r0 + k − 1 ≤ pn. Write HB for the full labeled paths of B through time T, and AB = V \ΠT (B). For all sufficiently large d (depending only on p), E L (ΠT (aj))k j=1 | HB  − Unif inj([k], AB)  TV ≤ kn−4 . (4.1) The same assertion holds with HB replaced by any coarser sigma field that determines AB. In particular it holds in the reverse cyclic coordinate order, and hence for the inverse permutation of a block of 2b complete sweeps, with the base paths observed in that reversed process. The empty-list error is zero.
